questions: Did you suffer a recent blow to your face?
Are you currently seeing double vision?
Do you have numbness or tingling in your cheeks, upper lip, or upper gums?
Has your vision become blurry or significantly worse?
Did you lose consciousness at the time of injury?
Do you experience pain when you try to move your eyes?
Is it difficult to breathe through your nose?
Have you vomited since the injury occurred?
Do you take any blood-thinning medications?
Are you experiencing a severe headache?
orders: CT scan of the facial bones and orbits with thin axial and coronal cuts
Visual acuity testing using a Snellen chart at bedside
Pupillary light reflex examination checking for a relative afferent pupillary defect
Exophthalmometry (Hertel) to assess for enophthalmos or proptosis
Forced duction test on the more restricted eye to assess for mechanical entrapment
Anterior nasal examination with a speculum to check for a septal hematoma
Fluorescein staining of the cornea with Seidel test to rule out globe rupture

dx_raw:
DIAGNOSIS: Traumatic entrapment of the inferior rectus muscle in a left orbital floor "blowout" fracture

Alternatives:
1. Orbital floor fracture without true muscular entrapment, with diplopia secondary to periorbital edema and hematoma
2. Medial orbital wall (lamina papyracea) fracture with medial rectus entrapment
3. Zygomaticomaxillary complex (tripod) fracture with disruption of the orbital floor
